focus: correctness and traceability - commandOnlyMentioned normalization and the wrapper invariance test

findingDetails.title: A markdown wrapper the normalizer does not strip turns a refusal or question into an offer
findingDetails.evidence: The strip chain drops backticks, asterisks, double quotes and only opening or closing single quotes, while COMMAND_GAP_WORDS at line 363 admits only plain words and apostrophes between a lead and the name. A bracketed, parenthesized, struck-through, HTML-tagged, guillemet or linked command keeps punctuation that blocks the anchored lead test at lines 444-450, so commandOnlyMentioned returns false and attachCommand offers the mutating command. Verified on all 12 refusal/question fixture rows across six wrapper pairs (72/72 flip) with 0 mismatches for the six covered pairs.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Ran the module's exported function over the 23 PLAIN_ROWS cross six non-normalized wrapper pairs: 72/72 refusal-question rows flipped, 0 request rows flipped, 0 mismatches for the six WRAPPERS pairs. The occurrence scan still finds the name inside the markup, so the failure is the lead match.
findingDetails.recommendation: Strip the markup wrappers the same way the existing marks are stripped, or let the lead gap ignore a short run of markup punctuation; extend WRAPPERS with the markdown set so the invariance test pins the whole class.

findingDetails.title: A doc-path mention of the command defeats a led refusal
findingDetails.evidence: The after-name lookahead blocks only [a-z0-9_-], unlike typedCommandIn's dot-and-slash continuation rule at line 234, so /create:readme.md and /create:readme/notes.txt count as occurrences. Every occurrence must carry a lead at line 439, so a led refusal plus an unled path reference returns false and attachCommand offers /create:readme.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The occurrence regex matches the name inside a .md file name and a directory segment; typedCommandIn already refuses both forms, so the two readers of the same prompt disagree on what a path is.
findingDetails.recommendation: Apply the same dot-and-slash continuation rule after the name that typedCommandIn uses, or skip an occurrence whose following characters make it a path.

results.summary: The branch diff is the two scope files and does what pass eleven's report says; F001 and F002 are new defects outside AC-007's enumerated marks.

The wrapper test pins the six listed marks and the retired-name mapping; F001 names the wrapper class it cannot see, F002 the occurrence-boundary disagreement with typedCommandIn.

noveltyJustification: Both findings are first-time (no prior iteration exists). F001 comes from running the exported mention guard over the test's own fixture rows with six wrapper pairs the test does not list; F002 comes from the occurrence boundary matching a doc-path reference that typedCommandIn already refuses. Neither repeats a recorded pass-ten or pass-eleven finding.
